sections.heading: QCOM — Qualcomm
sections.markdown:
**Signal / why now:** QCOM is #5 GLOBAL MOMENTUM (mom6 +40%) on a semis_ai factor — the AI/edge-silicon sleeve is entirely uncovered in the current GLOBAL card set (AMD and TXN cards both stand DISCARD on valuation), so this is a deliberate sector-rotation pick to re-cover the semis theme. It is the least-extended name in the sleeve: at ~$180 it is −27.6% off the 52w high (vs MU +532%/12m and AMD +210%), so the pattern is a mid-cycle re-rate, not a chase; regime is NEUTRAL and the US-demand-driven AI/edge revenue stream is not constrained by the BoP bookkeeping tilt.

**Archetype:** momentum_continuation (rate 0.50, up +30%, down −22%, 9mo). Method card: VAL_MOMENTUM_CONTINUATION. EV = +4.0%. Cross-archetype: no — semi cyclical, not defensive.

**3 questions a deep-dive must answer:**
1. How much of the mom6 +40% is the AI-edge/RF handset recovery vs Android market-share displacement by MediaTek — is the opex pivot (layoffs, Samsung lead-loss) structural or one-off?
2. At what mid-cycle EPS (handsets + IOT + auto) does QCOM trade optically reasonable — is the −27% off-high discount already pricing a normalizing cycle, or is the 6m move a short-cover?
3. Does the AI PC / data-center entry (acquired Assets) actually move the margin mix, or is it a long-dated call option that should not be double-counted in the valuation-anchored target?

**Fast-disqualify:** EV positive ✓ (+4.0%). Valuation target P/E-anchored to mid-cycle blended EPS, not spot semi-cycle — the −27% off-high entry leaves up-leg room ✓. Primary sources (QCOM 10-K/10-Q, hyperscaler & handset unit guidance, Android share data) identified and reachable ✓.
